claims.statement: For each original leaf tag v, writing I(T-v,z)=I(H_v,z)+zI(R_v,z) and q_j=i_j(H_v)-i_j(R_v), the favorable selector is q_(p+1)-q_p+r_(p+1)-r_(p-1)<0 while the selected aggregate term is q_p-q_(p-1). The resulting coefficient-operator mismatch identifies the additional selector-aware global inequality needed by a generating-function route; the claw-free independence-polynomial real-rootedness theorem does not provide it for arbitrary trees.
claims.scope: Retained as an exact local decomposition for every original leaf of a finite ordinary tree and a limited audit of the cited claw-free real-rootedness theorem. The mismatch identifies a missing comparison for this direct coefficient-comparison route, not a necessary step for all possible proof methods. This is a partial reformulation, not a proof or refutation of either registered identity.
claims.reason: retained. The polynomial split at the original support gives the claimed selector and summand identities with the correct zero-extended rank shifts; summing preserves distinct same-support leaf tags. The strict lower-region guard gives positive slack but no established selector-aware budget. Chudnovsky–Seymour Theorem 1.1 requires claw-freeness and establishes real-rootedness of individual independence polynomials; arbitrary target trees may contain an induced claw, and no coefficient-comparison bridge is given. The standing controls also show why local positivity cannot decide the complete sum. The claim remains partial and does not settle the primary target.

limitations: No proof or eligible counterexample for the lower-region ordinary-tree aggregate is established.
The cited theorem's hypothesis gap is checked; no broader literature survey or claim that no alternative theorem could help is made.
